_about.what: Years added after the Benefacts archive ends, from sources outside it.
_about.sign: Expenditure is stored negative, matching the Benefacts convention.
_about.caution: These figures come from the Charities Regulator's annual return, not from a full set of filed accounts. They are headline figures on the Regulator's own definitions and are not line-for-line comparable with the 182 fields Benefacts extracted. Where the two sources overlap they are not merged: the archive is left as it stands.
_about.grants: Individual State grant awards announced after the archive ends, recorded one award per row exactly as the awarding body published them. An award is the amount announced, not money shown as received in any set of accounts, so grants are listed beside the accounts and never added into them.

cra-ar.name: Charities Regulator — annual reports
cra-ar.licence: Open data, re-use of public sector information
cra-ar.notes: Bulk file. 83,051 annual report records. Employee and volunteer counts before 2021 are published as bands ('250-499') and are not used. From 2021 the Regulator collects full-time and part-time counts as integers; the employee figure here is their sum, a headcount, which is not the same measure as the average-employees figure in the Benefacts archive. Government funding is the sum of 'Income: Government or Local Authorities' and 'Income: Other Public Bodies', because charities reclassify between the two.

dcedy-lgbti-2024.name: Department of Children, Equality, Disability, Integration and Youth — 2024 LGBTI+ Community Services Funding Call
dcedy-lgbti-2024.notes: Press release announcing 24 projects: 15 under the 2024 LGBTI+ Community Services Funding Call (Scheme A €25,000–€100,000; Scheme B €5,000–€10,000) and 9 under the LGBTI+ Youth Fund 2024. Amounts are recorded to the cent as published.

probation-ar-2024.name: Probation Service — Annual Report 2024, Appendix 7
probation-ar-2024.notes: Appendix 7, 'Breakdown of funding streams for Community Based Organisations'. One row per organisation with three columns — Grant Funding, Additional Funding, Capital Funding — and a total; the table's own total is 'CBO Total Funding Spent in 2024', €18,951,340. Each column is recorded here as its own row. These are amounts the Probation Service reports as spent in the year, not awards announced in advance.

probation-ar-2025.name: Probation Service — Annual Report 2025, Appendix 8
probation-ar-2025.notes: Appendix 8, 'Community Based Organisations & 2025 funding'. One figure per organisation, with no split into grant, additional and capital funding and no total row, so it is not on the same basis as the 2024 table. The appendix states that additional 2025 funding went to community organisations for extra expenditure, new pilot initiatives and new services, some of which may cover spending in 2026; that additional funding is not itemised by organisation.

notes: Files with the Charities Regulator as Corlann, under the same charity number (RCN 20064853) as Brothers of Charity Services Ireland.
A 2025 return is also published, but its income, expenditure and surplus are identical to 2024 to the euro, so it is not used until the Regulator's figures are confirmed.

6247467.name: St. John of God Community Services CLG
notes: The 2022 return records no government income and €198.7m of trading and commercial income, against €179.6m and €216.6m of government income in the years either side. The government funding figure for 2022 is left blank rather than published as zero.

This is the operating charity. Its parent, Saint John of God Hospitaller Services Group (RCN 20106515), files an unconsolidated return of about €6m a year, which is why the Group's own entry is not extended.

1542030.name: Concern Worldwide
notes: Government funding here is the Regulator's category, which includes foreign governments and international public donors as well as the Irish State. It is not a measure of Irish State funding alone.
Employee counts are those reported to the Irish Regulator and do not include staff employed in the countries where Concern works.

6256716.name: GOAL
notes: Most of the government funding shown is the Regulator's 'other public bodies' category (€114m–€141m a year), which for an international NGO includes foreign governments and international donors. 'Government or local authorities' income, the closer measure of Irish State funding, is €11m–€15m a year.
Employee counts are those reported to the Irish Regulator and do not include staff employed overseas.

3047044.name: Tiglin Challenge
notes: Trading names include Tiglin, Teen Challenge (Ireland), Tiglin Therapeutic Community Ireland and Tiglin Day Centre.
The 2020 return gives income and expenditure only; assets, liabilities and staff numbers were not reported, so they are left blank. The return gives staff as a band of 50–249.
Gross income rose from €2.4m in 2021 to €6.5m in 2023 and €5.8m in 2024. Government and local authority income rose from €1.3m in 2021 to €4.9m in 2024.
2023 income includes €2.64m recorded as 'other sources', which accounts for most of that year's €2.83m surplus. The return does not say what it was.
Full-time staff fell from 59 in 2023 to 42 in 2024, while gross expenditure rose from €3.7m to €5.1m.

8222107.name: Peter McVerry Trust
notes: No 2024 annual return appears in the Charities Regulator file (effective 3 May 2026), so the record stops at 2023.
2023 shows a deficit of €11.4m, with expenditure of €70.0m against income of €58.7m. Net assets fell from €51.6m at end-2022 to €16.4m at end-2023.
Donation income fell from €15.1m in 2022 to €5.9m in 2023, while State income rose from €43.4m to €52.2m.
